newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Steady as buyer emerges, sparks hope.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Steady as buyer emerges, sparks hope.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil held steady despite falling swaps quotes as buying support emerged late Friday to support cash prices, traders said.
Late in the Asian trading day, two 20,000 tonnes cargo were sold by two majors to a Singapore-based trader at $100.00 and $101.00 per tonne respectively.
The cargoes were for loading in late July.
The trades sparked hopes that the market may be supported in in the near term. Traders were speculating that the buyer may be out to buy more fuel oil next week.
The buyer told Reuters that the company is looking to cover some of its short positions.
But North Asian sellers were less optimistic.
A Japanese trader said there are ample supplies in the market and the company is also finding it difficult to move its supplies.
Traders said the weak bunker market has also contributed to the poor fundamentals.
"The bunker volumes seems to have shrunk despite the fact that our prices are even lower than Rotterdam's", said one trader.
South Korean sellers were offering July fob Sout Korean barrels at below 20 cents discount to Singapore spot quotes.
Traders said reduced demand from China has aggravated the surplus situation.
The swaps market was discussed lower. July was last quoted at $98.00/$99.00 against Thursday's $98.50/$99.00.
August swaps were quoted at $97.75/$98.50 against $98.50/$99.00.
